## Overview

Because cellular automata over a group form a cartesian category, they can be
assembled with wiring diagrams: boxes for automata, wires for layers, with
splits where a layer is read twice and dead ends where it is discarded.
Catlab.jl writes such diagrams as programs (`@program`) over a presentation of
the boxes (`@present`). `realize` evaluates a diagram in the category of
cellular automata, and the result is a single automaton that runs on
CellularAutomataCore. This vignette rebuilds the host and aphid model of the
previous vignette as a diagram, then rewires it to add an intervention.

```{julia}
#| output: false
ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"
using CategoricalCellularAutomata
using Catlab: Catlab, @present, @program, FreeCartesianCategory, to_graphviz
using CellularAutomataCore: CellularAutomataCore, CAProblem, solve, ReferenceBackend
using Plots
```

## The boxes

The presentation names the layers (objects) and the updates (morphisms) with
their types. It says nothing about what the updates do:

```{julia}
#| output: false
pres = @present HostAphid(FreeCartesianCategory) begin
    H::Ob
    V::Ob
    infect::Hom(H ⊗ V, H)
    disperse::Hom(H ⊗ V, V)
    spray::Hom(V, V)
end
```

## A diagram

The model of the previous vignette updates the host from both layers and the
aphids from both layers. As a program, each layer is a variable, and reading a
layer twice is just using the variable twice:

```{julia}
model_diagram = @program pres (h::H, v::V) begin
    return (infect(h, v), disperse(h, v))
end
to_graphviz(model_diagram; orientation=Catlab.Graphics.LeftToRight)
```

The diagram copies both input wires, since each layer feeds both boxes.

## What the boxes do

The boxes are given as cellular automata over a 40 × 40 torus, the same rules
as before: a plant is infected when two or more aphids are on it, and aphids
breed on infected plants and spread from crowded cells. The spray halves the
aphid density, rounding down.

```{julia}
G = TorusGroup(40, 40)
H = FullShift(FinAlphabet(Int8[0, 1]), G)
V = FullShift(FinAlphabet(Int8[0, 1, 2, 3]), G)
X = otimes(H, V)
infect = CellularAutomaton(G, [(0, 0)], p -> begin
                               h, v = only(p)
                               return h == 1 || v >= 2 ? Int8(1) : Int8(0)
                           end; dom=X, codom=H)
nearest = [(0, 0), (1, 0), (39, 0), (0, 1), (0, 39)]
disperse = CellularAutomaton(G, nearest, p -> begin
                                 p[1][1] == 1 && return Int8(3)
                                 return Int8(max(0, maximum(q[2] for q in p) - 1))
                             end; dom=X, codom=V)
spray = CellularAutomaton(G, [(0, 0)], p -> Int8(only(p) ÷ 2); dom=V)
```

`realize` evaluates the diagram with these generators. The result is one
cellular automaton from `H ⊗ V` to itself, equal to the pair of the two
updates:

```{julia}
model = realize(model_diagram, pres; H, V, infect, disperse, spray)
(model == pair(infect, disperse), memory_set(model))
```

## Rewiring

To spray the field every day, before the plants and aphids are updated, the
aphid wire passes through the spray box first. The change is one line of the
program:

```{julia}
sprayed_diagram = @program pres (h::H, v::V) begin
    w = spray(v)
    return (infect(h, w), disperse(h, w))
end
to_graphviz(sprayed_diagram; orientation=Catlab.Graphics.LeftToRight)
```

The realised automaton is the composite of the spray, on the aphid layer only,
with the model:

```{julia}
sprayed = realize(sprayed_diagram, pres; H, V, infect, disperse, spray)
sprayed == compose(otimes(id(H), spray), model)
```

Both run on CellularAutomataCore, on any backend:

```{julia}
u0 = fill((Int8(0), Int8(0)), 40, 40)
u0[20, 20] = (Int8(1), Int8(0))
u0[10, 30] = (Int8(1), Int8(0))
runs = [solve(CAProblem(m, u0, 30); saveat=10) for m in (model, sprayed)]
(solve(CAProblem(sprayed, u0, 30); backend=ReferenceBackend()).u[end] == runs[2].u[end])
```

```{julia}
infected(u) = count(t -> t[1] == 1, u)
plot(heatmap(first.(runs[1].u[end]); c=[:palegreen, :darkred], clims=(0, 1),
             colorbar=false, aspect_ratio=:equal, framestyle=:none,
             title="untreated, day 30: $(infected(runs[1].u[end])) infected"),
     heatmap(first.(runs[2].u[end]); c=[:palegreen, :darkred], clims=(0, 1),
             colorbar=false, aspect_ratio=:equal, framestyle=:none,
             title="sprayed daily, day 30: $(infected(runs[2].u[end])) infected");
     layout=(1, 2), size=(800, 380))
```

Spraying halves the density of three on an infected plant to one, below the
two needed to infect a neighbour, so the infection never leaves the first two
plants.

## Mistakes are caught when a diagram is realised

Catlab's `@program` does not check that each wire carries the type its port
expects. Here the spray, which takes an aphid layer, is given the host layer,
and the program is accepted:

```{julia}
miswired = @program pres (h::H, v::V) begin
    return (infect(h, v), spray(h))
end;
```

The mistake surfaces when the diagram is turned into an expression of the
category, which is the first thing `realize` does; Catlab stops with an
assertion about mismatched ports:

```{julia}
try
    realize(miswired, pres; H, V, infect, disperse, spray)
catch err
    typeof(err)
end
```

A correctly wired diagram can still be given the wrong automaton for a box.
Here the spray box, whose wire carries aphids, is given an automaton on the
host layer, and composing it with the rest of the diagram fails:

```{julia}
host_spray = CellularAutomaton(G, [(0, 0)], only; dom=H)
try
    realize(sprayed_diagram, pres; H, V, infect, disperse, spray=host_spray)
catch err
    typeof(err)
end
```
